Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.migrations

Class Migrator

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.migrations.Migrator
public final class Migrator extends Object
Runs migrations and rolls them back, as Laravel's migrator does. 

 Migrator migrator = Migrator.builder(SQLiteSchema.of(db))
         .add(new CreateUsersTable())
         .add(new AddBioToUsers())
         .build();
 migrator.run();

Pending migrations run in name order. Each one runs in its own transaction when it asks for one and the database can undo schema changes; when it runs on the connection that holds the migrations table, its record is written in that same transaction, so the change and its record are kept or undone together. Otherwise the record is written right after the migration; a crash in between leaves the change applied and unrecorded, as in Laravel.

A failure stops the call with a MigrationFailedException; migrations before the failed one stay applied and recorded. A rollback or reset that reaches records whose migrations this migrator does not have is refused before anything is undone (MissingMigrationsException).

Every call refuses to start while one of the migrator's connections is inside a transaction, because nothing it recorded would be final until that transaction ends. Only one process should migrate a database at a time; plug a MigrationLock into the builder to enforce that.

Instances are immutable. Calls on one migrator are not meant to overlap.

    • fresh

      public List<MigrationResult> fresh()
      Drops every view and table of the default connection, the migrations table included, then runs every migration.

      Tables that no migration made are dropped too. Migrations of other connections are not touched until they run.

      Returns:
      what run() returns
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if a connection is inside a transaction
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the grammar cannot list or drop tables
      MigrationFailedException - if a migration fails
      QueryException - if a statement outside a migration fails

    • pretendRun

      public List<MigrationResult> pretendRun()
      Collects the SQL that run() would execute, without changing anything.

      The migrations table is read if it exists and never created. Inside pretend mode a migration that inspects the schema, for example with hasTable, sees nothing, so its SQL can differ from a real run.

      Returns:
      one result per pending migration, in order: MigrationResult.Outcome.PRETENDED with its SQL, or MigrationResult.Outcome.SKIPPED
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if a connection is inside a transaction
      MigrationChecksumException - if a migration that ran declares a different checksum than the one recorded
      MigrationFailedException - if a migration throws while its SQL is collected
      QueryException - if reading the migrations table fails

    • pretendRollback

      MigrationFailedException - if a migration throws while its SQL is collected

    • repairChecksums

      public int repairChecksums(List<Migration> migrations)
      Rewrites the recorded checksum of every migration that ran to the one it declares now.

      This is for recovery only: a local database that was never deployed, or a known accident. A deployed migration is changed with a new migration instead. Only migrations in the given list that ran and declare a checksum are touched; a migration that declares none keeps its recorded value. No migration event fires, and the call runs under the migration lock.

      Parameters:
      migrations - the migrations to repair, never null; usually migrations()
      Returns:
      how many records were rewritten, 0 when the migrations table does not exist
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if the list or an element is null
      IllegalStateException - if a connection is inside a transaction, or the migrations table has no checksum column
      QueryException - if reading or writing the migrations table fails

    • clearChecksums

      public int clearChecksums()
      Removes every recorded checksum, so no migration is checked until the next run records or adopts one again.

      Throws:

      QueryException - if reading or writing the migrations table fails
